method.mode: read-only audit; no repository data edited
method.selection: Explicit 85-row bounded inventory: stage 2 = 30 (10 per slot), stage 3 = 30 (15 per slot), stage 4 = 25 (all 13 merged lens artifacts, 7 image texture entries, 5 film emulation entries)
reviewed_surfaces: contextual_usage and existing-slot context extension provenance
out_of_scope: changing candidate identity based only on ID or slot name
method.important_limit: No claim of measured ranking or visual-quality improvement; recommendations require normal data/index/test workflow before runtime use.

intentional_specificity_no_change.reason: Preserve royal exile/future-rule specificity. It was present at introduction in a princess expansion, and tags/keywords independently establish royal ownership. A generic-looking ID is not authority to erase it.
Preserve blue-gray hanbok, silver-white thread and mountain/stream/pine/waterfall/wave details. Introduced together with modern_hanbok_valley_fullbody preset and core garment anchor.

Preserve robot casing, scratches/dents/serial marks and machine-use specificity. Introduced with robot presets and retains explicit robot proof/degree facets; object applicability permits depicting the machine as an object.
Preserve robot-casing ownership because robot_proof_family independently confirms it; no evidence that the general label is intended to erase that scope.
Preserve robotic limbs, drones and mecha shells; robot_proof_family independently supports domain ownership.
Preserve robot age/exposure/abandonment because robot_condition=decommissioned_abandoned and wear_decay prove authored specificity.
Preserve glass-or-lens ownership: ko, en and embedding all explicitly permit both. Do not reinterpret slot name as lens-only.
Preserve combined film halation plus soft light bloom: both labels explicitly declare that combination. It is a distinct authored candidate from the narrower lighting-cluster halation entry.
Preserve mild falloff and no solid border/local illumination replacement; these are directly visible extent/ownership conditions rather than unrelated substitutes.
Preserve selected-peripheral-edge extent and separation from scene illumination; this describes the actual ownership of the optical effect.
Preserve no direct eye contact: this is a geometric consequence of the closed-eye concept, not unrelated counterexample contamination.
